newsitem.title: UK: UK construction output rises 1.0 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: UK construction output rises 1.0 pct in 1996.

text.p: The total volume of UK construction output rose 1.0 percent in 1996 from 1995, the Department of Environment said.
In the fourth quarter of 1996, contruction output rose 1.0 percent from the previous quarter to its highest level for five years.
Growth in 1996 was mainly due to strong growth in the infrastructure, private commercial and private non-housing repair and maintenance sectors, the DOE said.
The second consecutive quarterly increase in the fourth quarter was caused by growth in the private housing, infrastructure, private commercial and private housing repair and maintenance sectors.
The total volume of new work in the fourth quarter of 1996 was three per cent higher compared with the previous quarter and three per cent higher compared with the same period a year earlier.
The total volume of repair and maintenance work was unchanged compared with the previous quarter and unchanged compared with the same period a year earlier.
New private housing work in the fourth quarter of 1996 was ten per cent higher compared with the previous quarter and 23 per cent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
New work in the public housing sector in the latest quarter was seven per cent higher than in the previous quarter but 15 per cent lower compared with the fourth quarter of 1995.
New infrastructure output in the fourth quarter of 1996 was five per cent higher than in the third quarter of 1996 and two per cent higher compared with the fourth quarter of 1995.

New construction work in the private industrial sector in the fourth quarter of 1996 was three per cent lower than in the third quarter of 1996 but unchanged compared with the same period a year earlier.
New private commercial output was two per cent higher compared with the previous quarter and nine per cent higher compared with the fourth quarter of 1995.

New work in the public non-housing sector (excluding infrastructure) in the fourth quarter of 1996 was five per cent lower than in the previous quarter and 13 per cent lower compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.

Housing repair and maintenance work (including improvement work) in the public sector was 16 per cent lower than in the previous quarter and seven per cent lower compared with the same period a year earlier.
Housing repair and maintenance work in the private sector was 12 per cent higher than in the previous quarter and six per cent higher compared with the same period a year earlier.

Repair and maintenance work in the public non-housing sector in the fourth quarter of 1996 was one per cent higher than the previous quarter but thirteen per cent lower compared with the fourth quarter of 1995.

Repair and maintenance work in the private non-housing sector in the latest quarter was unchanged compared with the previous quarter but 11 per cent higher compared with the same period a year earlier.
The seasonally adjusted number of employees in employment in January 1997 was two per cent lower compared with October 1996 and five per cent lower compared with January 1996.
Total employment (including the self-employed) in January 1997 was three per cent lower compared with October 1996 and four per cent lower compared with January 1997.
